title: Simulation tools and simulating computer systems
subtitle: From Python to GPSS, and using simulation to design the very machines that run it.

lang.title: Simulation languages and tools
lang.body: You can write a simulator in any language — Java, Python (SimPy), C++ — but dedicated tools save effort. GPSS models a system as transactions flowing through blocks (GENERATE, QUEUE, SEIZE, ADVANCE, RELEASE, TERMINATE). Commercial packages (Arena, AnyLogic, Simulink) add graphical building and animation. Whatever the tool, the core is the same: a clock, an event list, random streams and statistics collectors.

code.title: A queue simulator in code
code.body: Even a few lines of C++ give a working model. This program simulates a single-server queue with a deterministic pattern (arrival every 3 units, service of 2 each) and prints each customer’s wait — run it and step through with the DSA Lab.
code.steps: Arrival every 3, service 2 ⇒ the server is free before each arrival. Change the service time to 4: customer i starts at max(arrival, previous finish).

cpu.title: CPU and memory simulation
cpu.body: Computer architects evaluate designs before building them. A CPU simulator executes instructions and counts cycles; a memory simulator replays an address trace through a cache model. The scheduling chapter's Round Robin with quantum 4 yields an average wait of 5.67; a direct-mapped cache on the address trace 0 8 0 6 8 suffers 5 misses. Changing the parameters and re-running is exactly a simulation experiment.

net.title: Network simulation
net.body: Network simulators (ns-3, OMNeT++, Cisco Packet Tracer) model nodes, links, queues and protocols as discrete events: a packet arrives at a router, waits in a queue, is transmitted, propagates. A router output port is exactly an M/M/1-style queue: at ρ = 0.5 the simulated utilisation is 0.485 and the mean number in system 0.863.

tools.title: High-level system simulation
tools.body: Full-system simulators (gem5, QEMU) boot an operating system on a model of a computer, trading speed for detail — cycle-accurate is slowest. Choosing the abstraction level is the main design decision: the right model answers the question at the lowest cost.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• Simulation languages package the clock, event list, streams and statistics.
  • CPU, memory and network simulators are DES in disguise.
